title: Texas's 26th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 26th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Brandon Gill against Democratic nominee Steven Shook and Libertarian candidate Phil Gray. The district covers the northern Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs including Flower Mound, Lewisville, and most of Denton County, along with Cooke and Wise counties. Gill, first elected in 2024 after the retirement of longtime Rep. Michael Burgess, is a Trump-aligned conservative who serves on the House Judiciary, Oversight, and Budget Committees and is a member of the House Freedom Caucus. Shook, a nurse practitioner and North Texas native, is running on a platform focused on affordable healthcare, lowering prescription drug costs, and restoring accountability in government. The Cook Political Report rates this race as 'Solid Republican,' reflecting the district's strong conservative lean after Trump carried it by 24 points in 2024.
polling_note: No district-specific public opinion polls were found for Texas's 26th Congressional District race. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican.'

candidates.name: Brandon Gill
candidates.summary: Brandon Gill is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 26th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A Republican and member of the House Freedom Caucus, he serves on the Judiciary, Oversight, and Budget Committees, including the DOGE Subcommittee. Prior to Congress, he worked as an investment banker at Nomura Securities and founded the conservative news outlet DC Enquirer. His policy priorities include border security, mass deportations, reducing government spending, and opposing the Biden administration's policies.

candidates.name: Steven Shook
candidates.summary: Steven Shook is a nurse practitioner and the Democratic nominee for Texas's 26th Congressional District, having defeated Ernest Lineberger III in the March 2026 primary. A North Texas native and healthcare provider since 2009, he worked as a Trauma ICU nurse for 10 years before becoming a pulmonary critical care nurse practitioner. His 'People Over Politics' platform prioritizes affordable healthcare through a transition to universal coverage, lowering prescription drug costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and shifting school funding away from property taxes.

candidates.name: Phil Gray
candidates.summary: Phil Gray is a perennial Libertarian Party candidate running for U.S. House in Texas's 26th Congressional District. He has been a candidate in multiple election cycles and advocates for limited government and individual liberty. He is listed as a general election candidate alongside incumbent Brandon Gill and Democratic nominee Steven Shook.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists for this race, which caps confidence. However, the fundamentals strongly favor the Republican incumbent: Brandon Gill is the first-term incumbent in Texas's 26th District, which is described as a strongly conservative district where Donald Trump won by 24 points in 2024. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican.' Gill is a Trump-aligned House Freedom Caucus member with committee assignments on Judiciary, Oversight, and Budget. Democratic nominee Steven Shook is a credible healthcare-focused challenger who won his primary, but faces a significant structural disadvantage in a district that has not elected a Democrat in decades. The Libertarian candidate Phil Gray is a perennial candidate with limited vote share. With zero polling data and strong fundamentals pointing decisively toward the incumbent, a safe Republican rating with medium confidence is the appropriate informational forecast.
